proposal.title: Superscription
proposal.literary_form: framing title and attributed speech heading
proposal.deciding_marker: The words of Qohelet formula identifies the discourse that follows; 1:2 changes to a voiced thematic exclamation.
proposal.rejected_alternative: Reject 1:1-2 because the title and opening hebel declaration have different frame functions; retain 1:1-11 as an exact parent.
proposal.risk: high: voice and the attachment of 1:2 are disputed; this famous formula must not authorize speaker, editor, or authorship claims

proposal.title: Opening hebel and recurring-world poem
proposal.literary_form: thematic exclamation, profit question, and cyclic cosmological poem
proposal.deciding_marker: The hebel superlative and gain question open; generations, sun, wind, streams, weariness, recurrence, and failed remembrance close before first-person royal investigation.
proposal.rejected_alternative: Reject detaching 1:2 or 1:3 from the poem because the exclamation and question govern its cycles; retain 1:1-11 as the larger frame alternative.
proposal.risk: medium: stanza limits and the English rendering of hebel/yitron are uncertain

proposal.title: Royal wisdom inquiry begins
proposal.literary_form: first-person quest commission, observation, and provisional conclusion
proposal.deciding_marker: I Qohelet was king and I gave my heart reset the discourse; the wisdom/grief saying closes the first inquiry before the pleasure test.
proposal.rejected_alternative: Reject treating 1:12-18 as a self-sufficient final result; it is a distinguishable stage nested in the exact 1:12-2:26 investigation parent.
proposal.risk: high: investigation stages can be over-split and the royal persona cannot decide authorship

proposal.title: Pleasure, achievement, and possession experiment
proposal.literary_form: first-person experiment and achievement register with retrospective verdict
proposal.deciding_marker: Come now, I will test opens; the catalog of works and desires culminates in I turned to all my works and the no-profit verdict.
proposal.rejected_alternative: Reject atomizing pleasures, projects, possessions, and verdict; each belongs to one experiment, while 1:12-2:26 remains the governing parent.
proposal.risk: high: list-function and closure at 2:11 compete with the full investigation

proposal.title: Wisdom and folly under the common fate
proposal.literary_form: comparative reflection moving from advantage to death-leveling lament
proposal.deciding_marker: I turned to consider introduces a new comparison; hatred-of-life conclusion closes before the object shifts to toil and inheritance.
proposal.rejected_alternative: Reject ending at 2:16 because 2:17 is the affective conclusion; preserve 1:12-2:26 as the exact investigation parent.
proposal.risk: high: the common-fate reflection remains part of the larger royal inquiry

proposal.title: Toil, inheritance, and enjoyment conclusion
proposal.literary_form: toil lament, rhetorical questions, and gift/portion refrain
proposal.deciding_marker: I hated all my labor shifts the object to succession and anxious toil; the enjoyment/portion conclusion answers the movement and closes the 1:12-2:26 investigation.
proposal.rejected_alternative: Reject detaching 2:24-26 as an isolated maxim because it functions as the investigation's conclusion.
proposal.risk: high: refrain attachment, gift language, and 2:26 translation pressure require retaining the larger parent

proposal.title: Poem of appointed times
proposal.literary_form: balanced meristic time-pair poem
proposal.deciding_marker: For everything there is a season heads fourteen paired lines; peace closes the pair sequence before the profit question resumes.
proposal.rejected_alternative: Reject extracting individual time pairs; retain 3:1-15 and 3:1-22 as interpretive parent alternatives.
proposal.risk: high: chapter-coincident opening and famous-verse extraction could falsely privilege the poem apart from its reflection

proposal.title: Reflection on time, work, and the human horizon
proposal.literary_form: profit question, observation, enjoyment conclusion, and permanence reflection
proposal.deciding_marker: What profit has he who works resumes the discourse after the time pairs; recurrence/permanence conclusion at 3:15 closes before injustice is introduced.
proposal.rejected_alternative: Reject isolating 3:11 or the enjoyment refrain; both belong to the reflection, with 3:1-15 as a larger poem-plus-comment alternative.
proposal.risk: high: 3:11 is translation-dense and often extracted; the span coincides with the remainder of a chapter section but not a whole chapter

proposal.title: Injustice, mortality, and the portion question
proposal.literary_form: observed injustice, interior speech, human-animal mortality comparison, and enjoyment conclusion
proposal.deciding_marker: Moreover I saw introduces injustice; who can bring him back closes the mortality inquiry and its portion conclusion.
proposal.rejected_alternative: Reject separating judgment observation from mortality testing too confidently; retain 3:9-22 as the exact larger movement.
proposal.risk: high: 3:21 has translation/afterlife pressure and cannot be made a doctrinal seam

proposal.title: Oppression without comfort
proposal.literary_form: returning observation and threefold comparative lament
proposal.deciding_marker: Then I returned and saw opens a new observed social condition; dead, living, and not-yet-born comparison completes it.
proposal.rejected_alternative: Reject merging automatically with 3:16-22 merely because both concern injustice; 4:1 has a return formula, while the whole chapter remains an exact observation-cycle parent.
proposal.risk: medium: cross-chapter injustice continuation is plausible

proposal.title: Competitive toil and the paired hands
proposal.literary_form: observation, fool counterexample, and better-than saying
proposal.deciding_marker: Then I saw all labor shifts to rivalry; one handful with quietness resolves the two-hands contrast.
proposal.rejected_alternative: Reject isolating 4:6 as a free proverb; it concludes the rivalry/idleness contrast.
proposal.risk: medium: the solitary worker in 4:7-8 may extend the toil observation

proposal.title: Solitary toil and companionship
proposal.literary_form: returning observation, rhetorical lament, and benefit-of-companionship chain
proposal.deciding_marker: Then I returned and saw introduces the solitary worker; the threefold cord image closes the linked two-are-better chain.
proposal.rejected_alternative: Reject extracting the companionship sayings from the solitary-toil problem that they answer.
proposal.risk: high: famous-verse extraction at 4:9-12 and possible attachment to 4:4-6

proposal.title: Poor wise youth and unstable royal acclaim
proposal.literary_form: better-than saying expanded into succession and popularity observation
proposal.deciding_marker: Better is a poor and wise youth opens a new comparison; later generations' lack of rejoicing closes the political reversal.
proposal.rejected_alternative: Reject interpreting the figures as identifiable historical rulers or splitting the narrative illustration from its better-than heading.
proposal.risk: high: pronoun/referent ambiguity and a possible discourse continuation into worship counsel

proposal.title: Guarded worship, speech, and vows
proposal.literary_form: imperative temple/vow counsel with dream-word conclusion
proposal.deciding_marker: Guard your steps marks a sustained second-person imperative turn; fear God closes the speech/vow chain.
proposal.rejected_alternative: Reject cutting at the English chapter boundary as authority or detaching vows from guarded speech; record the WEB/MT mapping without selecting a preferred numbering.
proposal.risk: high: chapter/versification seam, obscure dream wording, and fear language require external Hebrew review

proposal.title: Hierarchy, wealth, loss, and the enjoyment portion
proposal.literary_form: power observation, wealth-saying chain, grievous case, birth-death comparison, and refrain conclusion
proposal.deciding_marker: If you see oppression shifts from worship to political-economic observation; the God-given portion and occupied heart close the movement.
proposal.rejected_alternative: Reject isolating 5:18-20 because it answers the wealth/loss movement; retain 5:8-6:12 as the larger wealth-and-appetite parent.
proposal.risk: high: chapter-coincident ending and enjoyment-refrain attachment are T467-sensitive

proposal.title: Possession without enjoyment and unfilled appetite
proposal.literary_form: grievous case, extreme-life comparison, appetite reflection, and closing questions
proposal.deciding_marker: There is an evil which I have seen opens a new case; who can tell what will be after him closes paired questions.
proposal.rejected_alternative: Reject chapter size as sufficient evidence; the case, appetite sayings, and questions form one movement, but 5:8-6:12 remains the exact larger parent.
proposal.risk: high: whole-chapter coincidence, obscure wording, and an equally defensible cross-chapter wealth unit trigger T467 deferral

proposal.title: Better-saying chain and balanced-day counsel
proposal.literary_form: linked better-than aphorisms, rebuke/corruption counsel, and concluding prosperity-adversity reflection
proposal.deciding_marker: A good name is better initiates the chain; consider God's work and paired good/evil days close it before autobiographical observation.
proposal.rejected_alternative: Reject atomizing each better-than proverb; preserve the complete chain and the whole-chapter wisdom parent.
proposal.risk: high: aphorism extraction and exact attachment of 7:13-14 are disputed

proposal.title: Extremes, mortality, and overheard speech
proposal.literary_form: first-person observation with paired prohibitions and practical rationale
proposal.deciding_marker: All this I have seen reopens observation; do not give your heart to all words and remembered self-knowledge close the counsel.
proposal.rejected_alternative: Reject extracting 7:16-18 as a freestanding ethical system; it belongs to the observed mortality and speech context.
proposal.risk: high: 7:16-18 is translation- and interpretation-dense and frequently decontextualized

proposal.title: Wisdom search and a difficult human-accounting conclusion
proposal.literary_form: first-person failed search, numbered finding, and summary claim
proposal.deciding_marker: All this I have proved by wisdom starts a renewed inquiry; behold, this only have I found closes with a general accounting claim.
proposal.rejected_alternative: Reject using gendered statements or hypothetical editor voices to decide the seam; preserve 7:1-29 and 7:23-8:9 as exact larger alternatives.
proposal.risk: high: rare syntax, gender language, numbered-saying form, and 8:1 attachment demand Hebrew and literary specialist review

proposal.title: Wisdom before royal power
proposal.literary_form: wisdom question, court imperative, time/judgment reflection, and observed power
proposal.deciding_marker: Who is like the wise man bridges into royal counsel; I have seen man rule over man closes the court-power observation.
proposal.rejected_alternative: Reject making 8:1 a chapter-authorized beginning or identifying the king historically; retain 7:23-8:9 as a larger wisdom-search alternative.
proposal.risk: high: 8:1 attachment, court-speech syntax, and time/judgment wording are contested

proposal.title: Burial, delayed justice, and enjoyment
proposal.literary_form: observed anomaly, proverbial reflection, counter-case, and enjoyment conclusion
proposal.deciding_marker: So I saw the wicked buried introduces the observed case; I commended mirth closes with the enjoyment response.
proposal.rejected_alternative: Reject detaching 8:15 from the justice anomaly it answers; preserve 8:10-17 as the larger justice/enjoyment/unknowability movement.
proposal.risk: high: textual difficulty at 8:10 and refrain attachment

proposal.title: Unsearchable work conclusion
proposal.literary_form: first-person inquiry and emphatic epistemic closure
proposal.deciding_marker: When I applied my heart resumes the quest formula; repeated cannot find out closes it.
proposal.rejected_alternative: Reject treating 8:16-17 as detached skepticism; it concludes the preceding movement and may extend through 9:1.
proposal.risk: high: cross-chapter continuation into 9:1 and a whole-chapter 8 parent are both plausible

proposal.title: Common fate and the imperative to live one's portion
proposal.literary_form: heart-applied reflection, common-fate observation, life/death comparison, and enjoyment/work exhortation
proposal.deciding_marker: For all this I laid to my heart resumes the prior inquiry; whatever your hand finds to do closes the sustained common-fate response.
proposal.rejected_alternative: Reject extracting 9:5-6 or 9:7-10 as doctrinal or motivational fragments; preserve the common-fate argument and its exhortation together.
proposal.risk: high: 9:1 cross-chapter attachment, 9:5-10 afterlife/theology pressure, and enjoyment-language translation

proposal.title: Chance and the net of time
proposal.literary_form: returning observation and animal-snare simile
proposal.deciding_marker: I returned and saw shifts from exhortation to outcomes not secured by ability; the evil-time net completes the image.
proposal.rejected_alternative: Reject merging automatically with the city parable; 9:11-12 has its own return formula and closed snare image, though 9:11-18 remains an exact parent.
proposal.risk: medium: the wisdom example at 9:13 may continue the same inability-to-secure-outcome theme

proposal.title: Poor wise man, forgotten deliverance, and wisdom sayings
proposal.literary_form: exemplary city narrative followed by comparative wisdom conclusions
proposal.deciding_marker: I have also seen wisdom introduces the example; one sinner destroys much good closes the linked evaluation.
proposal.rejected_alternative: Reject separating the wisdom conclusions from the narrative that demonstrates them; retain 10:1 attachment as an exact alternative.
proposal.risk: high: 10:1 may close the wisdom/foolishness comparison across the chapter seam

proposal.title: Small folly and disorder in rule
proposal.literary_form: folly comparison, court counsel, and ruler/servant reversal observation
proposal.deciding_marker: Dead flies and a little folly reopen the wisdom/folly contrast; servants on horses and princes walking close the social-reversal list.
proposal.rejected_alternative: Reject letting chapter numbering settle 10:1; it may conclude 9:13-18, while 10:1-7 coheres around small folly magnified in court and rule.
proposal.risk: high: 10:1 attachment and opaque court references

proposal.title: Hazard, skill, speech, and self-wearying folly
proposal.literary_form: occupational hazard chain transitioning to wisdom/speech contrasts
proposal.deciding_marker: He who digs a pit begins the work-risk sequence; the fool who cannot find the city closes the labor-and-speech folly chain.
proposal.rejected_alternative: Reject atomizing each hazard or speech proverb; the dull-iron skill pivot binds action and words in a larger chain.
proposal.risk: medium: exact pivot between 10:11 and 10:12 is contestable

proposal.title: Rulers, feasting, neglect, and guarded speech
proposal.literary_form: woe/blessing royal pair followed by household and secrecy sayings
proposal.deciding_marker: Woe to you, land initiates paired ruler evaluation; the winged messenger image closes the warning against cursing rulers.
proposal.rejected_alternative: Reject isolating royal, feast, money, and secrecy sayings; they form a court/household governance cluster.
proposal.risk: high: the cluster's internal logic and translation of 10:19 are disputed

proposal.title: Risk, uncertainty, and diligent action
proposal.literary_form: imperative wisdom chain built on uncertainty refrains
proposal.deciding_marker: Cast your bread opens the risk counsel; morning/evening sowing closes with the repeated you do not know rationale.
proposal.rejected_alternative: Reject extracting 11:1 as a single maxim or selecting one commercial/agricultural interpretation as seam authority; retain 11:1-12:8 as the broad life-course parent.
proposal.risk: high: rare imagery at 11:1, semantic uncertainty, and a chapter-opening T467 risk

proposal.title: Light, youth, remembering, aging, death, and closing hebel
proposal.literary_form: life-course exhortation flowing into an extended aging/death poem and frame refrain
proposal.deciding_marker: Light is sweet turns from sowing uncertainty to life-course joy and remembrance; 12:8 repeats the opening hebel formula and closes the Qohelet discourse before epilogue evaluation.
proposal.rejected_alternative: Reject cutting at the chapter boundary or extracting 12:1; the youth imperatives grammatically and rhetorically continue into the before-clauses and aging images.
proposal.risk: high: cross-chapter seam, aging metaphors, Creator/remember wording, 12:7 interpretation, and 12:8 frame voice all require specialist review

proposal.title: Epilogue: Qohelet's words evaluated and the matter concluded
proposal.literary_form: frame evaluation, wisdom-word metaphors, admonition, and final conclusion
proposal.deciding_marker: Further, because Qohelet was wise shifts to third-person evaluation; the end-of-the-matter and every-work conclusion closes the book.
proposal.rejected_alternative: Reject using a hypothetical editor identity to split 12:9-12 from 12:13-14; both function together as epilogue, while 12:8-14 remains an exact frame-overlap alternative.
proposal.risk: high: frame voice, one-shepherd wording, and final fear/judgment statements cannot decide authorship or theology

hardest_seams.reason: Title versus voiced thematic frame; speaker/editor identity must not decide attachment.
Several genuine experiment stages remain nested in one royal investigation whose refrains conclude rather than detach.
WEB/English and common MT chapter numbering place the worship/vow movement differently; numbering is not literary authority.
Wisdom-search conclusion and wisdom question may bind across the chapter edge; syntax and voice are difficult.
Applied-heart inquiry likely continues across the chapter edge into the common-fate observation.
The dead-flies aphorism can close the poor-wise-man wisdom/folly evaluation or open the chapter's court-folly cluster.
Youth imperatives, repeated before-clauses, aging images, dust/spirit closure, and hebel refrain form a cross-chapter life-course movement.
Closing hebel refrain belongs to the discourse frame while the third-person evaluation begins the epilogue; exact overlap alternatives remain.

t467_chapter_coincident_risks.assessment: Whole-chapter coincidence is supported by a grievous-case opening and paired closing questions, but 5:8-6:12 is an equally defensible larger wealth/appetite unit; keep LOW.
Preserved only as an exact parent, not proposed as one chunk; chapter numbering must not flatten distinct better-saying and investigation movements.
Preserved only as an exact parent; 8:1 and 8:16-17 have plausible cross-chapter attachments.
Preserved only as an exact parent; 10:1 may attach backward and the chapter contains multiple form clusters.
Rejected as the primary proposal because the poem begins with youth/light exhortation at 11:7; retain only as an exact conventional alternative.

oversplit_premortem: Do not detach an enjoyment refrain from the investigation, wealth observation, justice anomaly, or common-fate movement it concludes.
Do not atomize time pairs, achievements, better sayings, hazard sayings, ruler sayings, youth imperatives, or aging images below their governing rhetorical chain.
Do not let chapter boundaries decide 7:23/8:1, 8:16/9:1, 9:13/10:1, or 11:7-12:8.
Do not make Qohelet, frame voice, royal persona, gender shifts, or a hypothetical editor into boundary authority.
Do not force hebel, yitron, ra'ah, portion, spirit, judgment, or fear into one English or theological meaning to settle a seam.
